- tests/test_promote_main_cycle.py:213-231 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The autouse module-scoped fixture changes the process-global `tempfile.tempdir` and restores it only in `finally`. Its exec probe also reads whatever `tempfile.tempdir` an earlier fixture left set, so the result depends on fixture order.
  WHY: Any code that reads `tempfile.gettempdir()` or uses default `mkstemp`/`NamedTemporaryFile` while the fixture is active gets the redirected `$HOME/promote-cycle-tests-*` path. Under pytest-xdist the results are non-deterministic, and best-effort cleanup can leak scratch directories. Severity disagreement: minimax rated MAJOR, glm rated NIT; the highest is used.
- tests/test_promote_main_cycle.py:213-231 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: An `autouse=True` module-scoped fixture runs for every test without any test opting in. Its only effect is to change the process-wide `tempfile.tempdir`, and the file is not in the `files_touched` grant.
  WHY: This is implicit execution with no documented gate or invocation guard. It widens the effective scope beyond what the PR declares.
- tests/test_promote_main_cycle.py:219-225 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="promote-cycle-tests-", dir=home)` into `$HOME` has no exception handling. The guard checks only `isdir`, not whether `$HOME` is writable or a symlink to /tmp.
  WHY: A missing, read-only or noexec `$HOME` raises an uncaught `PermissionError`/`FileNotFoundError`/`OSError` during fixture setup, so every test in the module errors. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 explicitly declined this finding: mkdtemp runs only after `isdir(home)` and a successful exec probe inside home.
- tests/test_promote_main_cycle.py:201-231 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Fixture setup runs up to two subprocess probes, each with a 30s timeout, plus probe-script writes, a chmod and temp-dir create/teardown on every module run.
  WHY: This adds CI wall-clock time and I/O for a workaround that adds no coverage and fixes none of the module's failing tests.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:7258-7264 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `_linked_scope_step_name` does not specifically handle a job whose longest step is also its first failed/timed-out step, so script paths may be collected twice.
  WHY: The reviewer says this is not a runtime failure, only redundant logic that de-duplication makes harmless. The reviewer stated no severity, so the ledger defaults it to low.
